name: dotnet-channels

Deep guide to `System.Threading.Channels` for high-performance, thread-safe producer/consumer communication in .NET: `Channel<T>` creation (bounded/unbounded), backpressure, capacity, `IAsyncEnumerable`, graceful shutdown/drain, and hosted services. See [skill:dotnet-background-services] and [skill:dotnet-csharp-async-patterns].

`Channel<T>` is thread-safe with separate `ChannelWriter<T>`/`ChannelReader<T>` endpoints. Bounded channels are preferred for production: `Channel.CreateBounded<T>(capacity)` caps memory and supports `FullMode`; unbounded `Channel.CreateUnbounded<T>()` grows without limit and can exhaust memory. Unbounded -- use only when you control the producer rate.

`FullMode`: `Wait` (default; `WriteAsync` waits), `DropOldest`, `DropNewest`, `DropWrite` (`TryWrite` returns `false`). Use drop modes for telemetry/rate limiting/non-blocking overflow detection. Starting in .NET 7, `itemDropped` supports metrics, logging, or resource cleanup: `(item as IDisposable)?.Dispose();`

Use `await writer.WriteAsync(item, cancellationToken);` for backpressure and `writer.TryWrite(item)` for non-blocking writes. Multiple producers may write concurrently without external locking. Call `Complete()` or `TryComplete()` when no more items will be produced; `TryComplete` is idempotent. `writer.TryComplete(new InvalidOperationException("Source failed"));` propagates errors.

Preferred consumer:
`while (await reader.WaitToReadAsync(cancellationToken))`
`while (reader.TryRead(out var item))`
`await ProcessAsync(item, cancellationToken);`
It drains available items before awaiting. `ReadAsync` is simpler. Multiple consumer tasks scale processing; each item is read by exactly one consumer. `BackgroundService` consumers use `Task.WhenAll`, cancellation, scoped handlers, and error logging.

`await foreach (var item in reader.ReadAllAsync(cancellationToken))` integrates `IAsyncEnumerable`; completion exits after draining. ASP.NET Core streaming can return `reader.ReadAllAsync(ct)`. `System.Linq.Async` enables `.Where(...).Buffer(50)`.
